newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares wilt in thin turnover.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares wilt in thin turnover.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Thursday on what dealers called a miserable day, with little trade interest and thin turnover in the top shares.
"Friday looks like being a hesitant market but there may be continued interest in SAS, which rose nicely today and could go up further," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index fell 1.67 point to 183.86, in overall bourse turnover of 1.4 billion crowns, of which only about 0.5 billion was in top 20 paper.
The KFX August future fell 1.85 point to 183.25 with 1,262 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Following its better than forecast half-year results on Wednesday it got a further boost on Thursday from news that it was taking over sales for partner Lufthansa in Norway and Sweden and was working on a similar deal for Denmark.
Heading in the opposite direction was Novo Nordisk, which tumbled 17 crowns to 695.00 following a downgrade of CSFB's recommendation to 'hold'.
Den Danske Bank fell 15 crowns to 712.00 for no particular reason that dealers could see. The bank issues its first half report next week.
